questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: If $\sec\theta+\tan\theta=k$, then $\dfrac{k^{2}+1}{k^{2}-1}=$
questions.explanation: Since $\sec^{2}\theta-\tan^{2}\theta=1$, we have $(\sec\theta+\tan\theta)(\sec\theta-\tan\theta)=1$, so $\sec\theta-\tan\theta=\dfrac{1}{k}$. Adding and subtracting: $\sec\theta=\dfrac{k^{2}+1}{2k}$ and $\tan\theta=\dfrac{k^{2}-1}{2k}$. Hence $\dfrac{k^{2}+1}{k^{2}-1}=\dfrac{\sec\theta}{\tan\theta}=\dfrac{1/\cos\theta}{\sin\theta/\cos\theta}=\dfrac{1}{\sin\theta}=\csc\theta$.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: If $\sec\theta + \tan\theta = k$, then $\dfrac{k^2+1}{k^2-1} = ?$
questions.explanation: Since $\sec^2\theta - \tan^2\theta = 1$, we have $(\sec\theta+\tan\theta)(\sec\theta-\tan\theta)=1$, so $\sec\theta-\tan\theta = \tfrac1k$. Adding and subtracting: $\sec\theta = \dfrac{k^2+1}{2k}$ and $\tan\theta = \dfrac{k^2-1}{2k}$. Therefore $\dfrac{k^2+1}{k^2-1} = \dfrac{\sec\theta}{\tan\theta} = \dfrac{1/\cos\theta}{\sin\theta/\cos\theta} = \dfrac{1}{\sin\theta} = \csc\theta$.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: From a distance of $60$ m on the level ground, the angle of elevation of the top of a building is $45^\circ$ and the angle of elevation of the top of a flagstaff situated on the top of the building is $60^\circ$. Then the length of the flagstaff, in metres, is
questions.explanation: Let the observation point be $60$ m from the foot of the building. Building height $= 60\tan45^\circ = 60$ m. Height of the top of the flagstaff $= 60\tan60^\circ = 60\sqrt3$ m. Length of flagstaff $= 60\sqrt3 - 60 = 60(\sqrt3 - 1)$ m.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: In a triangle $ABC$, $AB = 5$ cm, $BC = 6$ cm and $CA = 7$ cm. Then the length of the median $AD$ (from $A$ to the midpoint $D$ of $BC$), in cm, is
questions.explanation: The length of the median from $A$ to side $BC$ is given by $AD^2 = \dfrac{2AB^2 + 2AC^2 - BC^2}{4}$. Substituting: $AD^2 = \dfrac{2(25) + 2(49) - 36}{4} = \dfrac{50 + 98 - 36}{4} = \dfrac{112}{4} = 28$. So $AD = \sqrt{28} = 2\sqrt7$ cm.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: In a triangle $ABC$, $AB = 6$ cm, $BC = 7$ cm and $AC = 11$ cm. If $AD$ is the altitude from $A$ to the side $BC$, then the length of $BD$, in cm, is
questions.explanation: The signed projection of $B$ on line $BC$ from the foot of the altitude uses $\cos B = \dfrac{AB^2 + BC^2 - AC^2}{2\cdot AB\cdot BC} = \dfrac{36 + 49 - 121}{2\cdot6\cdot7} = \dfrac{-36}{84} = -\dfrac37$. Then $BD = AB\cos B = 6\cdot\left(-\tfrac37\right) = -\dfrac{18}{7}$; the negative sign only means the foot $D$ lies outside segment $BC$ (the triangle is obtuse at $B$). The length $BD = \dfrac{18}{7}$ cm.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: If the lengths of the diagonals of a rhombus are $48$ cm and $14$ cm, then the perimeter of the rhombus, in cm, is
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, so half-diagonals are $24$ cm and $7$ cm. A side $= \sqrt{24^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{576 + 49} = \sqrt{625} = 25$ cm. Perimeter $= 4 \times 25 = 100$ cm.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: If the lengths of the two parallel sides of a trapezium are $18$ cm and $12$ cm and its area is $105\ \text{cm}^2$, then the distance between the parallel sides, in cm, is
questions.explanation: Area of a trapezium $= \tfrac12(a + b)h$, where $a, b$ are the parallel sides and $h$ the distance between them. So $105 = \tfrac12(18 + 12)h = 15h$, giving $h = 7$ cm.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: If the radii of two circles are $6$ cm and $18$ cm and the distance between their centres is $9$ cm, then the number of common tangents that can be drawn to the two circles is
questions.explanation: Compare the centre distance $d = 9$ with the radii. The difference of radii is $18 - 6 = 12$. Since $d = 9 < 12 = R - r$, one circle lies entirely inside the other without touching. Two circles in this configuration have no common tangents, so the answer is $0$.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: A chord of length $8$ cm of a circle subtends an angle $30^\circ$ at a point on the circumference of the circle. Then the length of the diameter of the circle, in cm, is
questions.explanation: By the extended law of sines, a chord and the inscribed angle it subtends satisfy $\dfrac{\text{chord}}{\sin(\text{inscribed angle})} = 2R = \text{diameter}$. So diameter $= \dfrac{8}{\sin30^\circ} = \dfrac{8}{1/2} = 16$ cm.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: If $A(5, 2)$, $B(6, -15)$, $C(0, 0)$ are the vertices of $\triangle ABC$, then $\triangle ABC$ is
questions.explanation: Compute the squared side lengths: $AB^2 = (6-5)^2 + (-15-2)^2 = 1 + 289 = 290$; $AC^2 = 5^2 + 2^2 = 29$; $BC^2 = 6^2 + 15^2 = 261$. Since $AC^2 + BC^2 = 29 + 261 = 290 = AB^2$, the triangle is right angled (at $C$). The three sides $\sqrt{29}, \sqrt{261}, \sqrt{290}$ are all different, so it is not isosceles — it is simply right angled.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: What is the ratio in which the $y$-axis divides the line segment joining the points $A(12, -3)$ and $B(3, 6)$?
questions.explanation: Let the $y$-axis ($x = 0$) divide $AB$ in the ratio $k : 1$ (from $A$ to $B$). By the section formula, $x = \dfrac{k(3) + 1(12)}{k + 1} = 0 \Rightarrow 3k + 12 = 0 \Rightarrow k = -4$. So the ratio is $-4 : 1$ (the negative sign indicates external division).

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: The ratio in which the $y$-axis divides the line joining the points $A(-4, 5)$ and $B(3, -2)$ is
questions.explanation: Let the $y$-axis ($x = 0$) divide $AB$ in the ratio $k : 1$ (from $A$ to $B$). By the section formula, $x = \dfrac{k(3) + 1(-4)}{k + 1} = 0 \Rightarrow 3k - 4 = 0 \Rightarrow k = \dfrac43$. So the ratio is $\dfrac43 : 1 = 4 : 3$.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: The equation of the line passing through the points $A(2, 1)$ and $B(4, 5)$ is
questions.explanation: Slope $m = \dfrac{5 - 1}{4 - 2} = \dfrac42 = 2$. Using point $A(2,1)$: $y - 1 = 2(x - 2) \Rightarrow y = 2x - 4 + 1 = 2x - 3$.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: The sum of $x$ and $y$ intercepts of the line $7x + 4y = 56$ is
questions.explanation: $x$-intercept (put $y = 0$): $7x = 56 \Rightarrow x = 8$. $y$-intercept (put $x = 0$): $4y = 56 \Rightarrow y = 14$. Sum $= 8 + 14 = 22$.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: The equation of the straight line which is inclined at an angle of $120^\circ$ to the positive $X$-axis and makes a $y$-intercept of $7$ units is
questions.explanation: Slope $m = \tan120^\circ = -\sqrt3$, and $y$-intercept $c = 7$. Line: $y = -\sqrt3\,x + 7$, i.e. $y + \sqrt3\,x - 7 = 0$.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: If the line $y = mx + c$ is the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining the points $A(4, -7)$ and $B(-2, 1)$, then $\dfrac{m}{c} = ?$
questions.explanation: Slope of $AB = \dfrac{1 - (-7)}{-2 - 4} = \dfrac{8}{-6} = -\dfrac43$, so the perpendicular bisector has slope $m = \dfrac34$. Its midpoint is $\left(\dfrac{4 + (-2)}{2}, \dfrac{-7 + 1}{2}\right) = (1, -3)$. Line through $(1,-3)$ with slope $\tfrac34$: $y + 3 = \tfrac34(x - 1) \Rightarrow y = \tfrac34 x - \tfrac{15}{4}$, so $c = -\tfrac{15}{4}$. Hence $\dfrac{m}{c} = \dfrac{3/4}{-15/4} = -\dfrac{1}{5}$.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: If the equation of the line joining $(2, 1)$ and $(-4, -5)$ is $ax + by + c = 0$, then $a + b = ?$
questions.explanation: Slope $= \dfrac{-5 - 1}{-4 - 2} = \dfrac{-6}{-6} = 1$. Line: $y - 1 = 1\cdot(x - 2) \Rightarrow x - y - 1 = 0$, so $a = 1$, $b = -1$. Thus $a + b = 0$. (Any scalar multiple of the equation gives the same $a + b = 0$.)

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: The mean of the following $50$ observations is: $1, 3, 5, 7, \ldots, 99$.
questions.explanation: These are the first $50$ odd numbers, forming an arithmetic progression from $1$ to $99$. The mean of an AP equals the average of the first and last terms: $\dfrac{1 + 99}{2} = 50$.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: The mean of $6$ observations is $40$. If one observation is excluded, then the mean of the remaining $5$ observations becomes $39$. The excluded observation is
questions.explanation: Sum of $6$ observations $= 6 \times 40 = 240$. Sum of remaining $5$ observations $= 5 \times 39 = 195$. Excluded observation $= 240 - 195 = 45$.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: The arithmetic mean of $24, 4, 12, 8, 36, 48, 20, 16, 28, 32, 40$ and $k$ is $26$. Then $k = ?$
questions.explanation: There are $12$ values. Sum of the given $11$ values $= 24 + 4 + 12 + 8 + 36 + 48 + 20 + 16 + 28 + 32 + 40 = 268$. Mean $= \dfrac{268 + k}{12} = 26 \Rightarrow 268 + k = 312 \Rightarrow k = 44$.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: Let $A = \{a, b, a + b, a - 4b, ab, 2b\}$. If $b > 6$ and the mean of the set is $b + 3$, then the median is
questions.explanation: Sum of elements $= a + b + (a+b) + (a-4b) + ab + 2b = 3a + ab = a(3 + b)$. Mean $= \dfrac{a(3+b)}{6} = b + 3$. Since $b + 3 \ne 0$, this gives $a = 6$. The six values are $6,\ b,\ 6+b,\ 6-4b,\ 6b,\ 2b$. For $b > 6$ the ascending order is $6-4b < 6 < b < 6+b < 2b < 6b$. The median (average of the 3rd and 4th values) $= \dfrac{b + (6 + b)}{2} = \dfrac{2b + 6}{2} = b + 3$.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: The median of a data containing $33$ observations is $71$. If another $4$ observations $98, 89, 63, 36$ are included in the data, the median of this new data is
questions.explanation: For $33$ observations, the median is the $17$th value $= 71$. Adding $98$ and $89$ (both $> 71$) and $63$ and $36$ (both $< 71$) gives $37$ observations, whose median is the $19$th value. The two smaller additions push the original median value $71$ from position $17$ to position $19$, while the two larger additions sit above it. So the $19$th value is still $71$; the median remains $71$.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: Four entries are added to the data $5, 28, 15, 10, 15, 8, 24$. If there is no change in the arithmetic mean and median but its mode is increased by $1$, then the four entries (quantities) that are added to the original data are
questions.explanation: Original data ($n = 7$): sum $= 105$, mean $= 15$; sorted $5, 8, 10, 15, 15, 24, 28$ so median $= 15$ and mode $= 15$. After adding $4$ entries, $n = 11$; unchanged mean $15$ needs new sum $165$, so the added entries sum to $60$. Only $12, 16, 16, 16$ sums to $60$. New data sorted: $5, 8, 10, 12, 15, 15, 16, 16, 16, 24, 28$ — median (6th value) $= 15$ (unchanged) and mode $= 16$ (three $16$s beat two $15$s), i.e. increased by $1$. All three conditions hold, so the entries are $12, 16, 16, 16$.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem:
The mode of the following frequency distribution is nearly:

| Family size | 1–3 | 3–5 | 5–7 | 7–9 | 9–11 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Number of families | 9 | 10 | 4 | 4 | 3 |
questions.explanation: The modal class is $3$–$5$ (highest frequency $10$). With $L = 3$, $f_1 = 10$, $f_0 = 9$ (preceding class), $f_2 = 4$ (following class), $h = 2$: mode $= L + \dfrac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2}\,h = 3 + \dfrac{10 - 9}{20 - 9 - 4}\times2 = 3 + \dfrac{2}{7} \approx 3.29$.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: If a card is selected from a deck of $52$ cards, then the probability of it being a red faced card is
questions.explanation: Face cards are Jack, Queen and King. The red face cards are these three in hearts and three in diamonds $= 6$ cards. Probability $= \dfrac{6}{52} = \dfrac{3}{26}$.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: Two dice are thrown once. What is the probability of getting a total of $10$ on the faces?
questions.explanation: Total outcomes $= 36$. The pairs giving a sum of $10$ are $(4,6), (5,5), (6,4)$ — that is $3$ favourable outcomes. Probability $= \dfrac{3}{36}$.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Choose the word that best expresses the meaning of the given phrase.

**Disregard for other people is ______.**
questions.explanation: *Callousness* is the quality of being insensitive and showing a hard-hearted disregard for others' feelings. *Respect* and *concern* are the opposite of disregard, and *insult* is a specific offensive act rather than a general attitude of indifference. Hence the correct word is **callousness**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Choose the single word that means the following.

**Persuade by flattery or coaxing.**
questions.explanation: To *cajole* is to persuade someone to do something by sustained coaxing and flattery. *Caress* means to touch gently, while *threaten* and *warn* imply intimidation rather than flattery. The correct word is **cajole**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Choose the single word for the given description.

**One who rules the country by force.**
questions.explanation: A *dictator* is a ruler who wields absolute authority, typically seized and maintained by force. A *democrat* upholds rule by the people, a *demagogue* stirs popular emotion, and a *bureaucrat* is an administrative official. The correct word is **dictator**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Choose the word that best expresses the given meaning.

**Kindness or generosity in bestowing gifts or money is ______.**
questions.explanation: *Largesse* means generosity in giving, especially money or gifts. *Stinginess* and *smallness* denote the opposite, and *largeness* refers to physical size, not generosity. The correct word is **largesse**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Choose the single word for the given description.

**To look at something quickly and secretly, especially through a small opening ______.**
questions.explanation: To *peep* is to look quickly and furtively, typically through a narrow gap or small opening. *Spy* implies covert observation more broadly, *probe* means to investigate, and *espy* means to catch sight of something at a distance. The precise word is **peep**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem: Choose the most appropriate **synonym** of the word **'emulate'**.
questions.explanation: To *emulate* is to imitate or match another, striving to equal or copy their qualities — closest to **mimic**. *Surpass* and *augment* imply exceeding or increasing, and *inflate* means to blow up in size. The best synonym here is **mimic**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem: Choose the most appropriate **synonym** of the word **'stentorian'**.
questions.explanation: *Stentorian* describes a voice that is extremely loud and powerful — hence **thunderous**. *Pleasing*, *musical*, and *gratifying* all suggest agreeableness, which is unrelated to sheer loudness. The correct synonym is **thunderous**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem: Choose the most appropriate **antonym** of the word **'urbane'**.
questions.explanation: *Urbane* means suave, polished, and refined in manner. Its opposite is **uncouth**, meaning ill-mannered and unrefined. *Sophisticated* and *poised* are synonyms of urbane, and *rural* contrasts with 'urban' but not with the manner-related sense of 'urbane'. The correct antonym is **uncouth**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem: Choose the most appropriate **antonym** of the word **'conducive'**.
questions.explanation: *Conducive* means favourable or helpful in bringing about a result. Its opposite is **adverse**, meaning unfavourable or hindering. *Productive*, *competent*, and *fruitful* all carry positive, helpful connotations similar to 'conducive'. The correct antonym is **adverse**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form.

**By the time the boy entered the classroom, others ______.**
questions.explanation: The main clause is in the simple past ('entered'), so the blank needs a past-tense form describing an action in progress at that moment. *Were leaving* (past continuous) fits: the others were in the act of leaving when the boy entered. *Leave* and *have left* are present forms, and *will have left* is future perfect — none agree with the past-time frame. The answer is **were leaving**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form.

**English ______ in many countries in the world.**
questions.explanation: English is not the doer but the thing acted upon, so a passive construction is required, and the statement is a present general truth. *Is spoken* (simple present passive) is correct. *Was speaking* is active past continuous, *spoken* alone lacks an auxiliary, and *had been spoken* is past perfect passive — none suit a timeless present fact. The answer is **is spoken**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form.

**The minister ______ for New Delhi yesterday.**
questions.explanation: The adverb 'yesterday' signals a completed action at a definite past time, which calls for the simple past tense: **left**. *Has left* (present perfect) and *had been left*/*Has been left* (perfect/passive forms) do not go with a specific past-time marker like 'yesterday'. The answer is **left**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form.

**The old man ______ here for many years now.**
questions.explanation: The phrase 'for many years now' indicates an action that began in the past and continues up to the present, which requires the present perfect: **has lived**. *Had lived* is past perfect, *lived* is simple past, and *was living* is past continuous — none convey continuation into the present. The answer is **has lived**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Change the voice of the following sentence.

**The boy gave a surprise to his father.**
questions.explanation: In the active sentence the boy (subject) performs the action on 'a surprise', with 'his father' as the indirect object. Converting the indirect object to the passive subject gives 'The father was given a surprise by the boy', keeping the simple past tense. Option (1) changes the meaning and voice pattern, (2) shifts to past perfect and drops the agent, and (4) uses the past continuous passive, which alters the tense. The correct passive is **The father was given a surprise by the boy.**

options.label: The father received a surprise from his boy.
The father had received a surprise.
The father was given a surprise by the boy.
The father was being given a surprise by the boy.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition.

**I can testify ______ his honesty.**
questions.explanation: The verb 'testify' collocates with the preposition **to** when vouching for something ('testify to his honesty'). *For*, *on*, and *upon* are not the idiomatic prepositions used with 'testify' in this sense. The answer is **to**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition.

**My grandfather is hard ______ hearing.**
questions.explanation: 'Hard **of** hearing' is the fixed idiomatic phrase meaning partially deaf. The other prepositions — *on*, *at*, *off* — do not form the standard collocation. The answer is **of**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition.

**He jumped ______ the opportunity of going abroad.**
questions.explanation: 'Jump **at** something' is the idiom meaning to accept an opportunity eagerly. *On*, *for*, and *off* do not form this idiomatic phrasal expression. The answer is **at**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Choose the meaning of the underlined idiom.

**After retirement, he became a _couch potato_.**
questions.explanation: A *couch potato* is someone who spends a great deal of time sitting idly, typically watching television — that is, **a lazy person**. It does not refer to being active, physically hefty, or weak. The correct meaning is **a lazy person**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Choose the meaning of the underlined idiom.

**You have _to think big_ if you want to achieve anything.**
questions.explanation: To *think big* means to be ambitious and set high, far-reaching goals — that is, to **have ambitious plans**. It does not mean thinking excessively, thinking calmly, or settling for modest plans. The correct meaning is **have ambitious plans**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct article.

**Kalidasa is ______ Shakespeare of India.**
questions.explanation: When a person is likened to a famous figure ('the Shakespeare of India', 'the Newton of...'), English uses the definite article **the** before the proper noun to mean 'the counterpart of'. The indefinite articles *a*/*an* and the numeral *one* do not convey this idiomatic comparison. The answer is **the**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct article.

**I saw an old man near ______ bus stop.**
questions.explanation: The blank refers to a specific, identifiable bus stop, so the definite article **the** is required. *A* and *an* would introduce it as non-specific and 'a' would also clash with the following consonant, while the possessive *our* changes the meaning. The answer is **the**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition.

**As he did not pay the dues, the electricity has been cut ______.**
questions.explanation: 'Cut **off**' is the phrasal verb meaning to disconnect a supply such as electricity. *Up*, *of*, and *out* do not form the required phrasal verb in this sense. The answer is **off**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition.

**Our company is now ______ a firm footing.**
questions.explanation: '**On** a firm footing' is the fixed expression meaning in a stable, secure position. The preposition 'on' is used with 'footing'; *in*, *into*, and *at* do not form this idiomatic collocation. The answer is **on**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition.

**Gulliver's Travels is a book ______ children.**
questions.explanation: When a book is intended for a particular audience, the preposition **for** is used ('a book for children'). *Of*, *to*, and *upon* do not convey the sense of 'intended for'. The answer is **for**.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
We use the rules of _____ to exchange files over the internet.

(1) FTP/IP
(2) Hyperlink
(3) HTML
(4) HTTP
questions.explanation: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the set of rules used by web browsers and servers to request and exchange resources (files, web pages) over the internet. 'Hyperlink' and 'HTML' are not transfer protocols, and 'FTP/IP' is not a standard protocol name. Hence the correct answer is HTTP.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
World Wide Web was invented by _____.

(1) Tim Berners-Lee
(2) Vinton Gray Cerf
(3) Charles Babbage
(4) Robert Kahn
questions.explanation: The World Wide Web was invented in 1989 by the British computer scientist Tim Berners-Lee. Vinton Cerf and Robert Kahn are credited with the TCP/IP protocols (the internet), and Charles Babbage designed the early mechanical computer. Hence the correct answer is Tim Berners-Lee.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
A piece of data that is stored within a web-browser and retrieved at a later time is called a _____.

(1) Bug
(2) Cookie
(3) Hyperlink
(4) Hyperloop
questions.explanation: A cookie is a small piece of data that a website stores in the user's web browser so it can be read back later (for example, to remember login or preferences). A 'bug' is a program defect, a 'hyperlink' is a clickable link, and 'hyperloop' is a transport concept. Hence the correct answer is Cookie.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
DNS is the short form of _____.

(1) Disk Numbering System
(2) Data Number Sequence
(3) Domain Name System
(4) Digital Network Service
questions.explanation: DNS stands for Domain Name System — the internet service that translates human-readable domain names (like example.com) into numeric IP addresses. The other expansions are not what DNS abbreviates. Hence the correct answer is Domain Name System.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Which one of the following serves as a reference point that connects a particular page to other pages on the web?

(1) Reference
(2) Web link
(3) Referral code
(4) Hyperlink
questions.explanation: A hyperlink is a reference within a web page that, when clicked, connects (links) that page to another page or resource. 'Web link' is loose everyday phrasing and not the technical term, while 'reference' and 'referral code' do not describe this navigation element. Hence the correct answer is Hyperlink.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Making a list of a company's physical assets is known as _____.

(1) background check
(2) filing
(3) inventory
(4) credit check
questions.explanation: An inventory is a detailed list or record of a company's physical assets and stock. A 'background check' and a 'credit check' verify a person's or firm's history, and 'filing' means storing documents. Hence the correct answer is inventory.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
A contract that prohibits an employee from switching to a competing company is called _____.

(1) inception option
(2) business conduct manual
(3) non-compete agreement
(4) paralegal clause
questions.explanation: A non-compete agreement is a contract in which an employee agrees not to join or work for a competing company (usually for a set period). The other terms do not describe such a restriction. Hence the correct answer is non-compete agreement.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
A company's positive resources are considered as _____.

(1) assets
(2) liabilities
(3) contracts
(4) working capital
questions.explanation: In accounting, assets are the resources a company owns that have positive economic value. Liabilities are what it owes, contracts are agreements, and working capital is a specific difference between current assets and current liabilities. Hence the correct answer is assets.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
The movement of finished goods from production to the customer is _____.

(1) physical supply
(2) physical distribution
(3) supply chain
(4) conversion cycle
questions.explanation: Physical distribution refers to the activities involved in moving finished goods from the point of production to the final customer (transport, warehousing, delivery). 'Physical supply' covers inbound movement of raw materials, 'supply chain' is the whole network, and 'conversion cycle' is a production/accounting concept. Hence the correct answer is physical distribution.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
Individual ownership of a business is called _____.

(1) Cooperative society
(2) Joint trade agreement
(3) Partnership management
(4) Sole proprietorship
questions.explanation: A sole proprietorship is a business owned and run by a single individual. A cooperative society and a partnership involve several members/partners, and a 'joint trade agreement' is not a form of ownership. Hence the correct answer is Sole proprietorship.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
> Freedom and power bring responsibility. The responsibility rests upon this assembly, a sovereign body representing the sovereign people of India. Before the birth of freedom, we have endured all the pains of labour and our hearts are heavy with the memory of this sorrow. That future is not one of ease or resting but of incessant striving so that we may fulfil the pledges we have so often taken and the one we shall take today. The service of India means the service of the millions who suffer. It means the ending of poverty and ignorance and disease and inequality of opportunity. The ambition of the greatest man of our generation has been to wipe every tear from every eye. That may be beyond us, but as long as there are tears and suffering, so long our work will not be over. And so, we have to labour and to work, and work hard, to give reality to our dreams. Those dreams are for India, but they are also for the world, for all the nations and peoples are too closely knit together today for anyone of them to imagine that it can live apart. To the people of India, whose representatives we are, we make an appeal to join us with faith and confidence in this great adventure. This is no time for petty and destructive criticism, no time for ill-will or blaming others. We have to build the noble mansion of free India where all her children may dwell.

What is the 'sovereign body representing the sovereign people of India' referred to in the passage?

(1) The Parliament of India
(2) The Assembly of a state
(3) The Constituent Assembly of India
(4) The Constitution of India
questions.explanation: The speaker addresses 'this assembly, a sovereign body representing the sovereign people of India' — this is the Constituent Assembly of India, the body of elected representatives to whom the speech is made. It is not an ordinary Parliament, a single state assembly, or the Constitution (a document, not a body). Hence the correct answer is The Constituent Assembly of India.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
questions.stem:
> The most frightening aspect of malnutrition is that it is likely to cause permanent damage to the brain. Experiments carried out on animals suggest that brain damage due to malnutrition is irreversible. This may not be true of human beings. Nevertheless, known facts as well as results of tests conducted so far point to alarming conclusions. The human brain grows very fast. Three months before its birth, the child's brain weighs one-fourth of the adult's brain. In one year, the brain of the child is already 66 percent of the weight of the adult brain. At four years, the brain weighs 90 per cent and at eight the child's brain is the size of an adult's and there is no further increase. Quite obviously, the first four years are crucial for the development of the brain. And if the child suffers from malnutrition, the damage to the brain may well be permanent. Thanks to the systematic research of the National Institute of Nutrition, Hyderabad, we are able to address at least some aspects of the problem of malnutrition in this country. For instance, it was found that the addition of iodine in the lake-water salt consumed in the Sub-Himalayan region would go a long way to controlling goitre. Again, experiments made by the Institute reveal that inexpensive green leafy vegetables are a good alternative to eggs and butter as a rich source of Vitamin A.

When does the child's brain attain full growth?

questions.stem:
> The last few years have ushered in a harsh reality where crises are the norm rather than the exception. Pandemics, economic slumps and extreme weather events were once tail-end risks but all the three have hit South Asia in rapid succession since 2020. This is deeply distressing because the knowledge, skills and health that people accumulate — their human capital — is a critical source of the resilience that countries rely on for recovery. Globally, countries that have systems in place to support individuals and families before a crisis spikes can better protect their citizens during the crisis. Human development systems must be agile, resilient and adaptive. Such systems will help countries better respond to future shocks as well. Crises are unpredictable, and often present rapidly changing circumstances. A well-functioning system is one that can spring into action the moment a shock strikes, ensuring essential services such as health care and learning remain uninterrupted. Since services are provided by different individual sectors, human development systems must be able to coordinate efficiently across sectors. The road ahead for South Asia is rocky. A robust human development system would not only mitigate the damage but also help ensure lives and livelihoods are protected.

In recent times, South Asia has experienced _____.

(1) robust growth in human skills
(2) unforeseen upheavals
(3) surge in human capital
(4) growth in healthcare
questions.explanation: The passage says pandemics, economic slumps and extreme weather events — once rare 'tail-end risks' — have hit South Asia in rapid succession since 2020. These are sudden, unexpected crises, i.e. unforeseen upheavals. The other options describe positive gains the passage does not report. Hence the correct answer is unforeseen upheavals.
